title: Astrid and the Interior
premise: Isandro Zhou, a bridge inspector who measures everything and owns nothing, learns that the house where she spent one hidden childhood year is being auctioned by the state. Inside its sealed attic she finds a notebook written in her mother's hand — half diary, half coded confession — whose final sentence is untranslatable, or so everyone insists. As developers, estranged relatives, and an old family friend named Veyra circle the property, Isandro realizes the sentence names what her mother did to survive, and that whoever controls the translation controls the truth. To finish it, Isandro must stop being a tenant of her own life: she claims the house, publishes the sentence unfinished, and lets the world argue over it while she finally moves in.
about_author: Lior Iversen is the pen name of a former municipal surveyor who spent eleven years inspecting public infrastructure across three countries before turning to fiction. Their work examines how people inhabit structures — buildings, marriages, identities — they never quite believe are theirs.

chapters.title: Expansion Joints
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. On the Halvard Bridge she measures a crack exactly wide enough to fail, files the report, and goes home to a husband who asks about her day without listening. The beat: competent numbness, a woman fluent in tolerances but not in wants.

chapters.title: The Notice
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. A certified letter announces the auction of 9 Alder Row — the house from the single year her mother hid her there. Her husband calls it clutter; she drives past it twice at night. Beat: the past arriving with paperwork, refusing to stay sentimental.

chapters.title: A Tenant's History
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV, with flashback. She reconstructs the year at Alder Row through fragments: a mother who changed names like coats, a rule never to answer the door. Beat: childhood remembered as survival training rather than love.

chapters.title: Veyra at the Gate
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. A former neighbor and her mother's old confidante appears at the viewing day, warm and precise, warning Isandro off bidding while offering help. Beat: charm with a locked room behind it.

chapters.title: What the House Weighs
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. At the open inspection she finds the attic sealed with fresh screws — someone has been inside recently. She bids anyway, borrowing against the marriage without telling her husband. Beat: first act of ownership, reckless and quiet.

chapters.title: The Winning Number
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She wins the auction against a development consortium represented by a smooth man named Corben Hale. That night her husband discovers the second mortgage. Beat: victory that costs the floor she stood on.

chapters.title: Marriage in Millimeters
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, Isandro and husband Tomas. A cold negotiation over money becomes a confession of years each spent not asking questions. Beat: two tenants discovering they co-signed a lease neither read.

chapters.title: Attic Light
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She unscrews the attic hatch and finds her mother's notebook: daily entries ending in a final sentence written in a private cipher mixed with three languages. Beat: awe curdling into dread — the last page is addressed to whoever finds it.

chapters.title: Three Languages, One Lie
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She takes pages to a retired translator, Dagny, who decodes fragments: dates, sums of money, a name redacted on every page. Beat: the mother emerging as someone who paid terrible prices to keep them both alive.

chapters.title: Corben's Offer
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. The consortium offers triple value for the house, mentioning the attic specifically — too specifically. He knows something about what's up there. Beat: power revealing itself as knowledge, politely extended.

chapters.title: Veyra's Version
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV. She tells Isandro her own account of that year: that Isandro's mother informed on people to protect her daughter, and that Veyra was among the named. Beat: sympathy weaponized; every story now has a price tag.

chapters.title: The Redacted Name
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Cross-referencing dates, Isandro deduces the redacted name may be Veyra's brother — or Veyra herself. She stops sleeping. Beat: the investigator realizing she is investigating her own right to exist.

chapters.title: Load Test
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Back on the bridge, she falsifies nothing but hesitates over a marginal reading, then reports it honestly — the first decision she makes as an owner of her judgment. Beat: professional integrity becoming personal template.

chapters.title: Tomas Leaves the Lease
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. He moves out, not in anger but in arithmetic: he cannot live inside a debt taken for a dead woman's secrets. Beat: grief without villainy; the marriage measured and found within tolerance for neither.

chapters.title: Dagny's Warning
chapters.summary: Dagny's POV. The translator admits she worked for the same network decades ago and recognizes the cipher's origin — and warns that the final sentence is not a confession but an instruction. Beat: the ground tilting; decoding may be doing, not learning.

chapters.title: Night Visitors
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. Someone enters the house while she sleeps upstairs; nothing is stolen except one page. She installs locks, then realizes the page taken was the decoy she'd planted. Beat: hunter and hunted exchanging places.

chapters.title: The Consortium's File
chapters.summary: Hale's POV. Under pressure from above, Hale reveals the consortium's interest: the house sits on land records that could unravel a larger property scheme built on the same old network's paper trail. Beat: corruption shown as architecture — load-bearing and invisible.

chapters.title: Sentence, Unfinished
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She decodes the final sentence up to its last clause, which requires a key only her mother held: a word Isandro herself spoke as a child, which she no longer remembers. Beat: climax approaching through absence — the missing word is her.

chapters.title: What the Mother Paid
chapters.summary: Veyra's POV, final time. Confronted, Veyra confesses she took the page and gives it back, along with the memory Isandro lost: the child's word, spoken the night her mother chose betrayal over surrender. Beat: pity and fury fused; the price of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: The Whole Sentence
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. The completed sentence reads as both confession and absolution — naming every person her mother harmed and every reason, refusing to cancel either. Isandro photographs it and sends copies to everyone named, including herself. Beat: climax; truth released from custody.

chapters.title: Demolition Delayed
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs briefly. The file goes public; the consortium's scheme collapses under scrutiny, Hale resigns, and the city moves to preserve Alder Row as evidence. Beat: aftermath as aftershock — justice arriving bureaucratic, partial, real.

chapters.title: Owner, Occupied
chapters.summary: Isandro's POV. She repairs the expansion joints report backlog, signs the house into her own name alone, and writes the final line of her own notebook: a sentence only she can translate. Beat: resolution — a tenant no longer, living inside a truth she chose to carry.
